At RAN2#95b meeting [2], RAN2 had the following agreement: RAN2 agree to apply QMC solutions only in CELL_DCH state. In RAN2 discussion paper [3], we provide some background information on QoE Measurement Collection, because this feature was triggered from SA4 and some information are related to upper layers, e.g. QoE metrics. From RAN3 point of view, for any potential change, it is good to also provide background information so that companies may have a full picture on the whole solution or structure of this feature. QoE metrics: In legacy MDT, MDT measurements were defined. Similarly, QoE metrics are also needed and they have already been defined in TS 26.247 in SA4 (see the sections 10.4). QoE configuration and reporting: In legacy MDT, for MDT measurements, the network should firstly send the MDT configuration to the UE, and then the UE performs MDT procedures (immediate or logged MDT based on network configuration). If the reporting criteria are met, the UE will send the MDT reports back to the network. Similarly, QoE configuration and reporting procedures follow the same principle as legacy MDT, i.e. the network sends the QoE configuration to the UE and then the UE sends the QoE report back to the network if the reporting criteria are met. Overview of QoE Measurement Collection solution: Figure 1 is from Figure 5.6-2 in the TR 26.909 v0.5.0 in the RAN3 LS [4]. Figure 1: Overview of QoE Measurement Collection solution As shown in figure 1, for QoE configuration, O&M or Core Network can initiate QoE configuration; For QoE report, the UE will send QoE report to the RNC, and then the RNC forwards it to the TCE. Later the QoE server could get the QoE report from the TCE. Compared with the legacy MDT, there may be the following differences: - Measurements are collected in upper layers in UE side - The TCE sends the QoE report to the QoE server after collecting from the RNC

Based on RAN3 LS R3-174964, RAN2 defined a new RRC inter-node message in TS38.331 for SMTC information, considering future extension (eg. CSI-RS), the message is named as “MeasurementTimingConfiguration”. After RAN2_101bis meeting, based on CR R2-1806431, the detail parameters are initially finalized. In RAN2 spec (i.e., TS38.331), the structure of the MeasurementTimingConfiguration message is per frequency level as shown in the following figure: Figure 1 Structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration in 38.331 However in latest RAN3 spec TS 36.423 v15.1.0, the usage of MeasurementTimingConfiguration is illustrated in the following figure (e.g. take EN-DC X2 SETUP REQUEST message and EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE message as examples), which is per cell level. Figure 2 Structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration in 36.423 Then for cell specific X2 procedure, the whole structure becomes: Figure 3 Combined structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration As shown in Figure 3, RAN2 defines the inter-node message to contain a list of frequencies, and corresponding SMTC configurations, but the inter-node message is used under per Cell configuration in RAN3. Observation 1: MeasurementTimingConfiguration is configured per frequency in TS38.331, but it is configured per cell in TS36.423, which is misaligned. Observation 2: According to RAN2 and RAN3 specification, for a given cell, MeasurementTimingConfiguration can include a list of frequencies and corresponding SMTC configurations. In order to avoid misleading in RAN3 specification, for per-cell level information transmission, we can add more detail semantics description for the Measurement Timing Configuration IE to instruct the network implementation. Proposal 1: Add semantics description for the Measurement Timing Configuration IE in TS 36.423 to clarify that only the frequency and SMTC configuration of the corresponding cell is included, rather than a list of frequencies and SMTC configurations. Proposal 2: Change the IE description of Measurement Timing Configuration in TS 36.423 from “IE” to “RRC message”.

that the absence of IEs within the following two sections means “to maintain current status” unless otherwise specified or implied: - Section 9.3.1.310 “Multicast CU to DU RRC Information”; - Section 9.3.1.314 “Multicast CU to DU Common RRC Information”. However, there is a small misalignment within the two structures: one node can add or modify the two IEs by either structures, but it cannot release either IE by using the former structure, although it can release by using the latter structure. A straightforward way to resolve the misalighment is to separate the structure “CHOICE MTCH-NeighbourCell Information” in Section 9.3.1.315 and the IE “CHOICE ThresholdIndex Information” in Section 9.3.1.316 used in “common” signalling as individual sections, and to modify the type of the two IEs in Section 9.3.1.310 toward references to these two new individual sections. Proposal 2bis-b: We propose RAN3 to confirm support of gNB-CU indicating release of “RRC multicast MTCH neighbour cell information” IE and/or the “threshold index” by issuing a per-session message. A feasible solution is to modify the type of the two IEs in Section 9.3.1.310 toward references toward the CHOICE structures (of addmod/release) used in Section 9.3.1.315 and Section 9.3.1.316. Similar as what is proposed in proposal 2, we propose to update the CHOICE structure extendable in ASN.1 Proposal 2bis-c: In the ASN.1 part, the CHOICE structures are updated to be extendable.

(CMCC,HW), (ZTE), (CATT) - common subset of agreeable functionality? - split work, merge/revise if needed; check details (CATT) In the end of CB #29 in RAN3 #107-e, the different potential agreements were organised according to the support they received from different companies to “almost agreed”, when agreement was almost reached, and to “FFS” topics, when more opposition was observed. The following were “almost agreed” in the last RAN3 #107-e: Include a new IE, namely NR Cell PRACH Configuration, into the Served Cell Information NR IE in TS 38.423 and the Served Cell Information IE in TS 38.473 (FFS for TS 36.423). The NR Cell PRACH Configuration IE further contain two sub-fields: UL PRACH Configuration List and SUL PRACH Configuration List, both encoded as an NR PRACH Configuration List structure. The NR Carrier List IE and the frequencyShift7p5khz IE should be added per-UL/SUL. Following IEs should be included into the NR PRACH Configuration Item structure: an NR SCS (SCS of the carrier), MSG1-FDM, the PRACH Configuration Index, the MSG1 SCS (only when L=139) the Root Sequence Index, the Zero Correlation Zone Config, and the Restricted Set Config (only when L=839). One item was supported by 7 companies and received objection from 1 company: One NR PRACH Configuration List structure may contain multiple NR PRACH Configuration Item structures. The following are still FFS: It is FFS over the following two options: a) to include a locationAndBandwidth and a msg1-FrequencyStart into the NR PRACH Configuration Item structure; or b) to include one MSG1 Frequency Start from Carrier IE instead. It is FFS on whether the rootSequenceIndex-BFR IE should be encoded as a Root Sequence Index IE or as another IE. It is FFS over the following two options: a) to postpone the discussion over SSB-related parameters to Rel-17; or b) to include one SSB Positions In Burst IE per cell, and one SSB per RACH Occasion IE per NR PRACH Configuration Item structure. As a reminder, RAN3 #106 agreed the following on the conflict detection and resolution function: RACH configuration conflict detection and resolution function is located at the gNB-DU; details on assistance info exchanged between CU and DU are FFS gNB-DU needs to know the PRACH configuration of some or all cells neighbors to a cell subject to RACH configuration conflict, in order to effectively chose a new PRACH configuration for the cell in conflict Signaling of UE RACH Reports to the gNB-DU is needed In the rest of the sections, we are going to discuss the above potential agreements and express our views with respect to them.

{"chunk_id":"R3-262229-002","collection":"ran3_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["PML","CMCC"],"tdocNumber":"R3-262229","title":"Proposals on Data-driven AI/ML framework for 6G RAN"},"point_id":"18235664449128927234"}
ndling, Distributed AI, and Operator Governance [5]. The overview of the related high-level topics is shown in Table 2-1. Table 2-1 The overview of the 3 High-Level Topics from SA2[5]: High-Level Topic 1: Agentic & Distributed Architecture ("The Machine")[5]. Contributions: AI Agent & Orchestration NFs: Proposals for centralized agents (AIMF, INCF, Planning Agents) and hierarchical control. Distributed AI & Model Management: Proposals for AI-Native NFs, Federated Learning, and TF/IF separation. Futhermore, the overview of the 5 layers corresponding to the 3 High-Level Topics is shown in Table 2-2. Table 2-2 The overview of the 5-Layer AI Structure for 6G Architecture from SA2[5] The above summarized information from SA2 indicates that the 6G AI framework should adopt a hierarchical structure, in which Layer 1 and Layer 4 involved in the Agentic & Distributed Architecture ("The Machine") correspond to the centralized AI brain and the distributed AI foundation/infrastructure, respectively. The general hierarchical architecture is adaptable to handling all use cases including AI for Network and Network for AI. Observation 1: The 6G RAN AI/ML framework shall follow the principles of AI-native and general architecture. Furthermore, the principles of the 6G RAN AI framework should be subordinate to the overall AI architectural principles for 6G system and aligned with them. Therefore, the deployment locations of model training and inference within RAN shall follow the hierarchical functional architecture with centralized and distributed/federated AI functionalities. Proposal 1: RAN3 is requested to identify the high-level principle that 6G RAN AI/ML study shall focus on general AI/ML framework/architecture for all use cases, which shall be hierarchical with centralized and distributed/federated AI functionalities. Regarding network energy saving and energy efficiency aspects of AI functionality, TR 38.760-3 [4] defines the use case of AI/ML-based network energy saving, and TR 22.870 [6] defines AI energy-efficiency-related 6G use cases, including AI for network and network for AI, and brings energy efficiency requirements to the network nodes covering RAN, CN, and OAM.

documents.text: ndling, Distributed AI, and Operator Governance [5]. The overview of the related high-level topics is shown in Table 2-1. Table 2-1 The overview of the 3 High-Level Topics from SA2[5]: High-Level Topic 1: Agentic & Distributed Architecture ("The Machine")[5]. Contributions: AI Agent & Orchestration NFs: Proposals for centralized agents (AIMF, INCF, Planning Agents) and hierarchical control. Distributed AI & Model Management: Proposals for AI-Native NFs, Federated Learning, and TF/IF separation. Futhermore, the overview of the 5 layers corresponding to the 3 High-Level Topics is shown in Table 2-2. Table 2-2 The overview of the 5-Layer AI Structure for 6G Architecture from SA2[5] The above summarized information from SA2 indicates that the 6G AI framework should adopt a hierarchical structure, in which Layer 1 and Layer 4 involved in the Agentic & Distributed Architecture ("The Machine") correspond to the centralized AI brain and the distributed AI foundation/infrastructure, respectively. The general hierarchical architecture is adaptable to handling all use cases including AI for Network and Network for AI. Observation 1: The 6G RAN AI/ML framework shall follow the principles of AI-native and general architecture. Furthermore, the principles of the 6G RAN AI framework should be subordinate to the overall AI architectural principles for 6G system and aligned with them. Therefore, the deployment locations of model training and inference within RAN shall follow the hierarchical functional architecture with centralized and distributed/federated AI functionalities. Proposal 1: RAN3 is requested to identify the high-level principle that 6G RAN AI/ML study shall focus on general AI/ML framework/architecture for all use cases, which shall be hierarchical with centralized and distributed/federated AI functionalities. Regarding network energy saving and energy efficiency aspects of AI functionality, TR 38.760-3 [4] defines the use case of AI/ML-based network energy saving, and TR 22.870 [6] defines AI energy-efficiency-related 6G use cases, including AI for network and network for AI, and brings energy efficiency requirements to the network nodes covering RAN, CN, and OAM.

[CR CR0614 for 38.473] Reason for change: In the PWS Cancel there are two sections with wrong section numbers. These section numbers are already in use in another section. Summary of change: Renumber the two affected sections. Considering the special situation since the two sections are already in use elsewhere, after discussion with MCC, we propose to simply renumber the sections Impact analysis: Impact assessment towards the previous version of the specification (same release): This CR has an no impact under functional or protocol point of view. Consequences if not approved: Ambiguous section numbering in the spec.

{"chunk_id":"R3-233315-003","collection":"ran3_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["ZTE"],"tdocNumber":"R3-233315","title":"Summary of Offline Discussion on CB: # 4_QoEAreaScope"},"point_id":"16244255689817213022"}
The area scope issue in QoE field also occurs in LTE specs. Currently, the presence of the area scope IE is mandatory in both TS 36.413 and TS 36.423. Meanwhile, in SA5 specifications like TS 28.405, it clearly explains that: If the parameter is not present the QMC shall be done throughout the PLMN specified in PLMN target. Hence, misalignment exists between RAN3 LTE spec and SA5 spec. Serial contributions also provided for TS 36.413 and TS 36.423 to fix this misalignment. Similar to what RAN3 has done in MDT aspects, a PLMN wide option is added into the mandatory QoE Area Scope IE(CHOICE structure). Q2.1 Please provide your views on whether the misalignment exists between RAN3 LTE spec(e.g. TS 36.413, TS 36.423) and SA5 spec(e.g. TS 28.405). To be continue: Q2.2: If the answer in Q2.1 is yes, please provide your views on how to fix this misalignment. Q2.3: If the answer in Q2.1 is no, please provide your views on how does the receiver node handle the QoE configuration without area scope IE in S1AP and/or X2AP messages based on the current spec. Companies may provide any other issues in this section. Q3. Please provide any other views if any.
